title: Indra returns: the dreamer isn't the self either (8.9–8.10)
hook: halfway home, Indra sees the flaw: if the reflection is the self, it goes blind with the body; so he walks back, firewood in hand
tomorrow: Indra returns again: not even deep sleep

segments.voice: Yesterday: Prajapati, and two students who took a reflection in a pan of water for the self. Your line was the reflection isn't you. Week five of year two begins.

A conversation ends, and it went well. Then, about a block later, it hits. Wait. That doesn't make sense. The words replay, the hole gets bigger, and the walking stops. Keep going and let it go, or turn around and admit it didn't land? Indra, king of the gods, has just left his teacher content, and now he's standing on that sidewalk, halfway home.
screen: `FEELING GREAT, THEN A BLOCK LATER.` → `WAIT. THAT DOESN'T MAKE SENSE.` → `KEEP WALKING, OR TURN AROUND?`

segments.voice: On the road, before he reaches the gods, Indra thinks it through. If the self is that reflection, then when the body is well dressed, it's well dressed. When the body is blind, it's blind. When the body is lame, it's lame. When the body dies, it dies. I see nothing good in this. So he turns around and walks back to Prajapati with firewood in his hands, samit-pani, the sign of a student asking to be taught. You left content, Prajapati says. Why are you back? Indra tells him. It is so, Prajapati answers. I'll explain it further. Live here another thirty-two years. The king of the gods signs up for thirty-two more years because one answer didn't hold. Then comes the next teaching: the one who moves about happily in dreams, that is the self. Better, surely. The dreamer isn't blind when the body is blind, isn't lame when the body is lame. Indra leaves, content again. And again, on the road, the doubt comes. In dreams, it's as if someone is killing him, chasing him. It's as if he feels pain. He even weeps, as it were. I see nothing good in this either. So, once more, he turns around. Notice the pattern. Prajapati doesn't give the whole answer at once. He gives an answer good enough to test, and waits for the student to find its edge. The teaching isn't only in the answers. It's in Indra's willingness to walk back.
screen: `IF THE BODY IS BLIND, SO IS IT.` · `BACK, WITH FIREWOOD IN HAND.` · `THE DREAMER: SURELY THIS ONE?` · `BUT IN DREAMS, HE WEEPS.` · then, large: `NOT THE DREAM.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and notice the pictures that start on their own, a memory, a plan, a little scene, like a dream but awake. Don't follow them; notice that a picture is showing and something is aware of it, and when a scene pulls you in, step back to the one aware of the dream.
Indra returns. The king of the gods walks back to his teacher, twice, because the reflection and then the dreamer didn't hold up.
Your line: not the dream. Tomorrow, Indra goes back a third time. See you then.

howItsDone: Students in many Hindu traditions return to their teacher with questions again and again; carrying firewood (samit-pani) is the traditional sign of approaching a teacher as a student.

original.note: Sanskrit svapna: dream, dreaming. the second answer Indra tests and finds wanting.

trapdoor: what you thought: a story where the king of the gods keeps failing.
what it means: a model inquiry. each answer is tested until it breaks, and the student keeps coming back.
what a scholar hears: Chandogya 8.9–8.10, the second of Prajapati's stages; waking body, dream and deep sleep parallel the three states the Mandukya treats as one sequence.
recall: a raised open palm: don't be afraid

the king of the gods coming home to his throne
a demon king returning to fight the gods

chat.says: Why does Indra keep going back to Prajapati?
options: Each answer, tested on the road, didn't hold, so he went back to learn more.
Prajapati kept calling him back because Indra had failed his tests.
He forgot what he was taught and needed to hear it all once more.
chat.meaning: The reflection would be blind when the body is; the dreamer still weeps. Each time Indra finds the edge of an answer, he walks back.

Prajapati.meaning: lord of creatures, the teacher in this story

samit-pani.meaning: fuel in hand: the sign of approaching a teacher

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 8.10.1–4 (the dreamer; the doubt again)
